item.title: China and US Discuss AI, Investment on Second Day of Trade Talks
item.description: Chinese and US officials wrapped up their second day of talks in New York on Monday to discuss artificial intelligence, investment and trade as they sought to advance negotiations ahead of President Xi Jinping’s visit to the US this week.
item.dc:creator: Nectar Gan

item.title: Trump, Mamdani Meet Ahead of UN General Assembly
item.description: "Balance of Power" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Rep. Darrell Issa (R-CA), Vice Chairman of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, says he opposes a diesel export ban, but warns US oil producers against using higher global prices to boost profits while creating scarcity at home. Frank Cilluffo, Director of the McCrary Institute for Cyber and Critical Infrastructure Security at Auburn University, says the US will “never firewall” its way out of the cyber threat and needs to take more proactive steps against adversaries. Jozef Síkela, EU International Partnership Commissioner, says Europe is already the largest contributor to development assistance and is looking to mobilize more private capital for emerging and developing markets. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Vietnam Leader Says US Deal Close, Denies Re-Routing China Goods
item.description: Vietnamese President To Lam said his nation is “very close” to a trade deal with the US as he pledged to buy more high-tech goods like aircraft to narrow the trade gap ahead of talks with Trump administration officials in New York.
item.dc:creator: Francesca Stevens, Nguyen Dieu Tu Uyen, Nguyen Xuan Quynh and Haslinda Amin

item.title: Síkela Says Europe Looks to Expand Development Financing
item.description: Jozef Síkela, EU International Partnership Commissioner, says Europe is already the largest contributor to development assistance and is looking to mobilize more private capital for emerging and developing markets. Síkela says the EU’s partnership package with Greenland is aimed at strengthening security and resilience while creating jobs and economic value. Síkela says Europe wants to work with Canada to reduce critical-mineral dependence on China. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Cilluffo Warns Cyber Attackers Still Hold the Advantage in AI Era
item.description: Frank Cilluffo, Director of the McCrary Institute for Cyber and Critical Infrastructure Security at Auburn University, says the US will “never firewall” its way out of the cyber threat and needs to take more proactive steps against adversaries. Cilluffo says AI can strengthen defenders but warns that, for the foreseeable future, the initiative remains with attackers. Cilluffo also argues the US must keep human control over increasingly powerful AI systems while continuing to compete with China. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Kallas Urges EU to Bolster Red Sea Mission Against Houthi Threat
item.description: The European Union’s top diplomat, Kaja Kallas, called for member states to send more naval vessels to protect commercial shipping in the Red Sea.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Palasciano

item.title: Rep. Issa Warns Oil Companies Against Profiting From US Shortage
item.description: Rep. Darrell Issa (R-CA), Vice Chairman of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, says he opposes a diesel export ban, but warns US oil producers against using higher global prices to boost profits while creating scarcity at home. Rep. Issa calls the gains a “tremendous windfall,” and companies “can’t have it both ways.” Rep. Issa argues the US has mismanaged the Houthi threat for years, allowing the group to rebuild its capabilities and support attacks in the region. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Businessweek Daily: Oil Falls on Iran Hopes (Podcast)
item.description: Oil fell below $100, heading for its longest run of declines since June, as robust flows through the Strait of Hormuz and diplomacy around the US-Iran war tamed a recent rally. Satellite data showed that Saudi Arabia’s observed oil loadings from inside the Persian Gulf jumped over the weekend, with the highest number of ships seen at the nation’s main Persian Gulf port since June. Meanwhile, US President Donald Trump told Fox News he would “probably” be open to meeting his Iranian counterpart, Masoud Pezeshkian, on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York this week. Trump will also hold a summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping, and may meet leaders of Persian Gulf nations. Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, for its part, said it has prepared itself for a protracted war, state media reported. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Mamdani Presses Trump at Meeting on Status of Haiti Migrants
item.description: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani said he pressed President Donald Trump on the status of Haitian immigrants in the US during a meeting at Gracie Mansion.
item.dc:creator: Myles Miller and Cameron Fozi

item.title: World Leaders Converge on United Nations General Assembly
item.description: Oil fell below $100 as robust flows through the Strait of Hormuz and diplomacy around the US-Iran war tamed a recent rally. Meanwhile, President Trump told Fox News he would “probably” be open to meeting his Iranian counterpart on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly this week. We get reaction from Chris Kennedy of Bloomberg Economics. Karen Veraa-Perry, Head of iShares Fixed Income Strategy within BlackRock's Global Fixed Income Group, joins to talk markets. Toby Rice, President & CEO of EQT, joins for a look at natural gas' role in global energy flows. CNN, MS Now and Politico filed a lawsuit seeking to allow their journalists to enter the White House grounds days after President Trump revoked their access. We discuss Katie Fallow, Deputy Litigation Director at Columbia University's Knight First Amendment Institute. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Tech Stocks Rally as Oil & Treasury Yields Retreat
item.description: The Close brings you the latest news and analysis leading up to the final minutes and seconds before and after the closing bell on Wall Street. Today's guests are Mizuho Securities USA President & CEO Jerry Rizzieri, IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva, ABB Motion President Brandon Spencer, Tola Capital Founder & Managing Director Sheila Gulati, DoubleLine Capital Deputy CIO Jeffrey Sherman, Port of Long Beach CEO Dr. Noel Hacegaba, Salesforce Chief Ethical & Humane Use Officer Paula Goldman, Milwaukee Bucks President Josh Glessing, & Just Salad Founder & CEO Nick Kenner. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Vance Says ‘More Work to Do,’ Playing Defense in Senate Fight
item.description:
Vice President JD Vance urged North Carolina voters to give Republicans more time to accomplish their agenda as the GOP is on the defensive in key states ahead of November’s midterm election. Vance traveled to the battleground state on Monday in a bid to shore up support for Republican Senate candidate Michael Whatley, who polls show trailing Democratic former Governor Roy Cooper. The contest has morphed into an opportunity for Democrats to flip a crucial seat.
Bill Faries, Bloomberg News Senior Editor, joins to discuss the state of voter sentiment with less than 45 days until US midterm elections. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump White House Media Ban: Does It Violate the First Amendment?
item.description: President Donald Trump’s ban on CNN, Politico and MS NOW from the White House is headed to court, raising new questions about how far a president can go in restricting press access.
item.dc:creator: Georgia Fearn

item.title: Burnham Seeks ‘Sweet Spot’ Between Promoting and Regulating AI
item.description: Andy Burnham said the UK would seek to find the “sweet spot” between encouraging the development of AI and ensuring the safety of its use, as the British prime minister prepared to meet US President Donald Trump.
item.dc:creator: Chloe Chaplain

item.title: UK Confirms Burnham’s Former Fiefdom of Manchester to Host G20
item.description: The leaders of the world’s biggest economies will descend on Manchester next year after the UK government confirmed the English city will host the Group of 20 summit.
item.dc:creator: Chloe Chaplain

item.title: UK Urges Patience From Mauritius With Chagos Deal in Limbo
item.description: The UK has reassured Mauritius of its determination to pursue a plan to cede sovereignty over the Chagos Islands to the Indian Ocean nation, even as officials concede the handover could remain on ice until after US President Donald Trump leaves office.
item.dc:creator: Ellen Milligan, Kamlesh Bhuckory and Chloe Chaplain

item.title: Brazil Election: Lula and Bolsonaro Fight Over Milei’s Economy Before Vote
item.description: Two weeks before a tight presidential election, Brazil’s leading candidates have turned Javier Milei’s Argentina into a proxy for their own clashing economic visions.
item.dc:creator: Martha Beck

item.title: Jon Ossoff Is Proving Himself in Georgia
item.description: Senator Jon Ossoff is leading in the polls and dominating in fundraising. Bloomberg Opinion columnist Mary Ellen Klas went to Athens, Georgia to see if his constituents think the senator has what it takes to solve voters' concerns. (Note: Klas mispeaks at 0:03 as Ossoff is trying to hold the seat not flip it.) (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: CNN, MS NOW, Politico Sue Over Trump’s White House Press Ban
item.description: CNN, MS Now and Politico filed a lawsuit seeking to allow their journalists to enter the White House grounds days after President Donald Trump revoked their access, turning to the courts in their fight over constitutional protections for the press.
item.dc:creator: Madlin Mekelburg and Magan Crane

item.title: Microsoft CEO to Join OpenAI, Nvidia Bosses at Trump-Xi Meal
item.description: Microsoft Corp. Chief Executive Officer Satya Nadella is planning to attend a White House state dinner for Chinese President Xi Jinping this coming week, according to a person familiar with the planning, joining leaders at Apple Inc., OpenAI and Nvidia Corp.
item.dc:creator: Brody Ford
